newsitem.title: UK: British shops suffer 20 percent increase in crime.
newsitem.headline: British shops suffer 20 percent increase in crime.

text.p: British retailers suffered a 20 percent increase in robberies last year, despite a 450 million stg investment in crime prevention measures, according to a survey published on Tuesday.

The British Retail Consortium's annual crime cost survey said the overall cost of retail crime fell to 1.42 billion stg in 1996 from 1.5 billion in the previous year. But the level of crime still posed a major challenge.

During the year retailers suffered 5.3 million incidents, an average of 18 for every shop in the country. More than 9,000 staff were the victims of physical violence and 167,000 were threatened with violence or verbally abused.
Customer and staff theft accounted for 73 percent of all losses. The number of customer thefts fell by seven percent to 4.9 million, but still cost retailers 653 million stg.
Staff theft costs fell 14 percent to to 386 million stg, but the number of incidents rose 31 percent to 31,000. Nearly 20,000 staff were involved and 40 percent were referred to the police.
Retailer spending on security staff was higher than ever, at 46 percent of all expenditure on crime prevention measures.
The BRC, the British retail trade association, said its survey was based on 48,000 outlets with a combined turnover of 95 billion stg. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
